key_insight: Representation theory explains why diagonal SSM transitions cannot track noncommutative groups and motivates quaternion channels for order-sensitive memory.
engineering_relevance: HyperSSM preserves linear-time inference and parallel training while enabling compact, interpretable state tracking for noncommutative dynamics.
method: Model recurrent transitions as a linear representation of the input-sequence monoid.
Characterize group tracking through quotients of the transition-generated group and real, complex, and quaternion blocks.
Add quaternion channels to build HyperSSM and interpret learned transition weights.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact solutions to benchmark group tasks with at most five state numbers, including S5 with 32 generators, and generalization to sequences 25 times longer than training sequences.
watch_item: The abstract establishes results on structured state-tracking tasks, not broad language-model performance or practical throughput gains.
paper_title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
